fieldNotes.title: Teacup Window Leaf Watch
fieldNotes.useCase: A printable yard or park-edge page for helping a young writer turn one watched detail into a tiny Teacup Town story.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print the page, bring one pencil, choose a calm outdoor spot, set an eyes-only rule for living things, and keep the group together.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Stand or sit beside your adult. Choose one detail you can see from your spot and imagine how a tiny teacup neighbor would notice it.
fieldNotes.noticePrompt: I noticed one outdoor thing from my safe spot: ____________________.
fieldNotes.detailBankPrompt: Three soft details I can add are color ____________________, shape ____________________, and sound ____________________.
fieldNotes.storySeed: In Teacup Town, the window helper spotted ____________________ and thought it meant a tiny surprise was coming.
fieldNotes.sentencePath: First the helper saw ____________________. Then the teacup neighbor wondered ____________________. At last they decided ____________________.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Make one sentence clearer by adding a color or size detail here: ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: point to one detail, then write only three words about it: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, tell someone how the Teacup Town window clue became ____________________.

fieldNotes.title: Acorn Avenue Errand Clue
fieldNotes.useCase: A printable field note for turning one yard or park detail into a setting clue for an Acorn Avenue errand story.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print the page, bring one pencil, choose a calm yard or park bench area, and remind the child to observe without collecting items.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Pretend Acorn Avenue has a tiny errand office. Look for one ordinary outdoor clue that could change the day's message.
fieldNotes.noticePrompt: The outdoor clue I noticed for the errand office is ____________________.
fieldNotes.detailBankPrompt: The clue's color is ____________________, its texture looks ____________________, and it sits near ____________________.
fieldNotes.storySeed: The Acorn Avenue clerk found ____________________ on the errand shelf and had to send a careful message.
fieldNotes.sentencePath: The clerk needed ____________________, but the outdoor clue showed ____________________, so the new errand became ____________________.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Add one setting detail that tells where the clerk is standing: ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: draw a small box around your favorite clue word and copy it here: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, turn the errand clue into a two-sentence story about ____________________.

fieldNotes.title: Pocket Park Pattern Board
fieldNotes.useCase: A printable yard or park observation page for finding repeated shapes, colors, or sounds and turning them into a story clue.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print the page, use a clipboard if available, and choose a calm patch where the child can see repeated details without moving far.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Look for a pattern: same shape, same color, same spacing, or a repeated sound. Then pretend it belongs on the Pocket Park board.
fieldNotes.detailBankPrompt: The pattern repeats like ____________________, changes near ____________________, and makes the park feel ____________________.
fieldNotes.storySeed: On the Pocket Park board, someone left a pretend note that said the pattern of ____________________ was a secret story clue.
fieldNotes.sentencePath: I saw ____________________. It repeated when ____________________. My character used the pattern to decide ____________________.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Circle the plainest word in your story and replace it with a clearer pattern word: ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: make three tiny marks for the pattern, then name it here: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, ask someone to guess which pattern started the story: ____________________.

fieldNotes.title: Button Bakery Direction Mix-Up
fieldNotes.useCase: A printable field note for building a three-part story sequence from safe outdoor details near a yard, porch, or park seat.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print the page, bring one pencil, and choose an outdoor spot with three visible features such as a bench, planter, and tree.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Pretend the Button Bakery note got mixed up. Use three things you can see to build the order of the story.
fieldNotes.detailBankPrompt: My three story moments feel like quiet ____________________, silly ____________________, and surprising ____________________.
fieldNotes.storySeed: In Button Bakery, a mixed-up note sent the helper from ____________________ to ____________________ before the true clue appeared.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Add one why word so the order makes sense: because ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: number three outdoor details, then write the one that starts the story: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, retell how the Button Bakery helper fixed the mix-up with ____________________.
